subject.title: [Bug]: Hundreds of repeated HTTP requests to 169.254.169.254:80 for the first 10 minutes after the startup

question: Is the linked PR's source-level and no-signal runtime proof enough to land the Bedrock IMDS fix, or should maintainers require live sandbox plus explicit AWS default-chain credential proof first?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible and the fix path is focused, but accepting it changes provider credential probing behavior at an auth/security boundary that source tests cannot fully prove for all AWS setups.

options.title: Require live credential proof
options.body: Wait for or run one no-signal sandbox trace plus one explicit Bedrock AWS default-chain path, such as AWS_PROFILE or EC2/ECS, before merging the linked PR.

options.title: Accept source-backed proof
options.body: Merge the linked PR after exact-head CI if maintainers accept the AWS SDK source contract and contributor no-signal output as sufficient for this limited fix.

options.title: Choose a different fix shape
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask for a narrower or more compatibility-preserving Bedrock credential probe design if the linked PR's boundary is not acceptable.

recommendation.title: Require live credential proof
recommendation.body: Wait for or run one no-signal sandbox trace plus one explicit Bedrock AWS default-chain path, such as AWS_PROFILE or EC2/ECS, before merging the linked PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Most closely connected to the current pluginized memory embedding boundary and likely to decide the provider-compatibility proof bar.
